Marathon Petroleum stock dropped 5.3% today after climbing nearly $30 over the prior four trading days. The sharp reversal came as oil prices fell — U.S. crude tumbled below $100 a barrel on Monday (September 21st) after Trump signaled openness to talks with Iran, easing some of the geopolitical premium that had driven prices higher. For a refiner like Marathon, lower crude prices initially sound good, but the market may be pricing in concern that a de-escalation in Middle East tensions could persist, removing the supply-disruption fears that had lifted energy stocks.

The broader picture shows refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with healthy storage levels across crude, gasoline, and diesel — conditions that normally support refiner margins. However, the stock's reversal suggests traders are now focusing on the risk that diplomatic progress could stabilize global oil supply over the near term, which would undercut the margin expansion that benefited refiners last week when geopolitical risk was driving crude toward $130 globally.
